title: Compare creation masks
goal: Predict and verify ordinary file and directory permissions under three process-local masks.
challenge: Create ll-u6 and compare new ordinary files/directories with masks 0022, 0027 and 0077 in its home. Explain why masks remove bits rather than grant execute permission; existing objects and the learner shell must stay unchanged.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-u6 && ! getent group ll-u6 && test ! -e /home/ll-u6 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-u6
steps.explanation: Fail closed if this disposable name or home exists. -m creates a home from /etc/skel; -U creates a primary group; no password is set.
steps.expected: Fresh account ll-u6, same-named primary group, home and Bash shell. A nonzero status/collision means stop setup.

steps.command: umask; sudo runuser -u ll-u6 -- bash -c 'umask 0022; touch "$HOME/f22"; mkdir "$HOME/d22"; umask 0027; touch "$HOME/f27"; mkdir "$HOME/d27"; umask 0077; touch "$HOME/f77"; mkdir "$HOME/d77"'
steps.explanation: Each change occurs only in the child Bash. New files normally request 0666; directories 0777.
Result is requested bits AND the inverse mask, not decimal subtraction. The parent shell mask is unchanged.
steps.expected: All six predicted results; ordinary files lack execute.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-u6 -- bash -c 'umask 0000; touch "$HOME/f77"; stat -c %a "$HOME/f77"'
steps.explanation: Changing umask then touching an existing file does not change its mode.
steps.expected: f77 still 600; chmod would be needed for existing permissions.

hints: Write separate predictions for ordinary files and directories.
umask filters requested permissions; it cannot add execute to a 0666 request.
Keep experiments in a child shell to avoid changing later learner commands.
review: Six predicted/observed modes match; original f77 remains 600; parent umask unchanged.
No default ACL is set in this fixture; ACLs can change real creation behavior elsewhere.
coverage: LPIC-1 104.5 file creation mask. Partial coverage; original material, self-review only. No automatic assessment or full LPIC preparation.
